requirements.evidence: Prefix resolution is implemented (app/Models/Queue.php:24 DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP, :101-116 defaultPrefixFor with <=0/>=20/P fallback, :121-134 prefixForPriority with custom map), and the map is validated on every save (app/Models/Queue.php:38-50, :57-96: canonical keys, A-Z values, effective uniqueness incl. uncovered 0/10/20). Daily per-prefix sequencing is implemented (app/Models/Ticket.php:88-96 filters issue_date and matches ^PREFIX(\d{3,})$, skipping malformed/legacy A codes; app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:44-48 reads the clock once; factory app/database/factories/TicketFactory.php:59-73 uses priority + day). issue_date migration with nullable-add/backfill/change/index swap/down exists (database/migrations/2026_09_13_000000_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:12-35). UpdateQueue gained ?array $priorityPrefixMap (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:21) with null/[]/validate semantics and ValidationException (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:58-67). Docs/changelog updated (docs/business-rules.md:78, docs/database-schema.md:101,117,164, CHANGELOG.md:25). However app/Models/Queue.php:13 adds priority_prefix_map to #[Fillable], directly contradicting requirement 2 ('not mass-assignable from user input'); and the down() in the issue_date migration re-adds unique(queue_id, code) after dropping issue_date, which fails if two days share a code (database/migrations/2026_09_13_000000_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:24-29).

conventions.evidence: Domain write still goes through the Action and keeps Gate::forUser(...)->authorize (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:58-67); migrations have down() (database/migrations/2026_09_13_000000_...:24-35, ..._000001_...:21-28); docs kept in sync in the same change (docs/business-rules.md:78, docs/database-schema.md:101,117,164, CHANGELOG.md:25), matching conventions.md:92-103. Deviations: the project requires a test for everything implemented (conventions.md:13-21) and none were added; import order is broken/unused at app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:5 ('use InvalidArgumentException;' inserted between App\Models\Queue and App\Models\User, while the catch uses \InvalidArgumentException), so Pint ordered_imports/unused would fail; app/Models/Queue.php:13 puts a task-declared non-mass-assignable field in #[Fillable], contrary to 'Set $fillable/$guarded deliberately' (conventions.md:46); database/migrations/2026_09_13_000001_...:12-14 uses a hand-rolled Schema::hasColumn guard that make:migration does not generate and the sibling migration does not use.

security.evidence: Authorization is preserved: Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue) remains the first statement (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22) and the new map path is validated (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:61-65) with the model hook as a backstop (app/Models/Queue.php:38-50). Codes/issue_date use forceCreate with trusted values (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:52-61) and the map is JSON-cast, so no new output/escaping surface. The weakness is mass-assignment: app/Models/Queue.php:13 makes priority_prefix_map fillable, so any future Queue::create()/update() fed from request data can set the map without going through UpdateQueue's authorization; the task explicitly forbids this (task.md:31-32), and the factory requirement does not need it (factories force-fill / can use forceFill in afterMaking).

tests.evidence: The only test file touched is tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php, and every hunk is an assertion rename A->N (tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:26, :39-40, :54, :82, :604, :609, :617-620, :631-636, :644). No test was added for custom maps / Queue::validatePriorityPrefixMap, daily restart, per-prefix independence, the UpdateQueue priorityPrefixMap parameter and its ValidationException/no-change behaviour, factory code allocation for a past issued_at, or the migration. Requirement 6 and the UpdateQueue action have no coverage at all, and none of the new failure paths is exercised, so per conventions.md:13-21 ('No production code without a test') this is not done.

simplicity.evidence: app/Models/Ticket.php:35-80 turns nextCode into a mixed-argument dispatcher that accepts a Queue/int/prefix/date in the second position, parses date strings via Carbon with try/catch (:43-47, :58-79), while both call sites pass exactly (queueId, prefix, Y-m-d) (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:48, database/factories/TicketFactory.php:73); that branching is speculative and makes the sequence logic unnecessarily hard to verify. The same issue_date-from-issued_at block is duplicated (app/Models/Ticket.php:122-137 and database/factories/TicketFactory.php:41-53). Dead branches remain in app/Models/Queue.php:63-70 (! is_array on a ?array parameter, and the null key case) and the map is validated twice on the UpdateQueue path (:61-62 and :48).

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short except nextCode (app/Models/Ticket.php:35-96), which mixes three input modes and date parsing. app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:50-51 now says 'System-set fields (code/status/issued_at/issue_date) are not fillable by design' while app/Models/Ticket.php:21 adds issue_date to the fillable list, so the comment is false. database/factories/TicketFactory.php:42-53 and :68-71 carry duplicated branching. Test names are stale: 'skips a malformed latest code instead of colliding on A001' (tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:78) and 'continues the sequence past A999' (:147 region) still describe the old codes.

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the ticket: actions (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php), models (app/Models/Queue.php, app/Models/Ticket.php), the two migrations, the two factories, the three required doc files (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md) and the affected test. No unrelated refactors, formatting churn or new features; the out-of-scope UI/totem work is absent.

issues.explanation: priority_prefix_map is added to the model's #[Fillable] list, contradicting requirement 2 ('The map is not mass-assignable from user input') and creating a write path that bypasses UpdateQueue's authorization; factory support does not require it.

No test was added for any new behaviour (map validation, daily restart, per-prefix independence, UpdateQueue's priorityPrefixMap/ValidationException, factory allocation by issued_at day, migration); the file only renames existing A-codes to N-codes, so the project's test-first rule is not met.

nextCode was turned into a mixed-parameter dispatcher (Queue|int|prefix|date, Carbon parsing, try/catch) even though both callers pass (queueId, prefix, 'Y-m-d'), adding speculative branching that obscures the actual sequence rule.

down() re-adds unique(queue_id, code) after dropping issue_date, which fails whenever the same code exists on more than one day (e.g. N001 today and N001 tomorrow), so the migration is not reliably reversible.
The new use InvalidArgumentException is out of alphabetical order and unused (the catch uses the fully-qualified name), so Pint's ordered_imports/unused-import rules would flag the file.
The 12-line 'derive issue_date from issued_at (or today)' block duplicates app/Models/Ticket.php:122-137; a single shared helper would keep the two paths from drifting.
The comment states issue_date is not fillable by design, but app/Models/Ticket.php:21 adds it to the fillable list, so the comment is misleading.
Because the parameter is typed ?array, the is_array($map) check and the $keyString === null branch are unreachable dead code.
The Display code line mentions priority prefixes but not the new queue-level priority_prefix_map, its canonical-key/letter format or uniqueness rules, so the new domain invariant is undocumented.
The hand-written Schema::hasColumn guard is not something make:migration generates and is inconsistent with the sibling issue_date migration, which has no such guard.
Test descriptions still refer to the old A001/A999 codes while the assertions expect N-codes, making failures harder to interpret.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based prefixes, the per-queue prefix map with model-side validation, daily per-prefix sequences, the issue_date migration and the UpdateQueue parameter, and updates the three required docs. It is not approvable as is: it exposes priority_prefix_map to mass assignment against an explicit requirement, and it adds no tests for any new behaviour. Secondary problems are an over-engineered mixed-argument nextCode, duplicated date logic, a down() that can fail, and Pint-breaking imports.
